published_statement: p.18: 'Theorem IV.1. Let f be any real-valued test function compactly supported in a small sampling domain. Let l^mu be a null vector field defined in the neighbourhood of support of f. Then, for all Hadamard states psi  <:rho_n:(f^2)>_psi >= -2 INT_D d^n alpha/(2pi)^n ((Q x Q)W_0)_kappa(fbar_alpha, f_alpha) - xi <:phi^2:(Q[f])>_psi, (72) where W_0 is the two-point function of the reference Hadamard state psi_0 and Q = l^mu nabla_mu.' With (69b) Q[f] = nabla_mu nabla_nu(l^mu l^nu f^2) + (1/2) R_mn l^mu l^nu f^2, f_alpha(x) = e^{i alpha x} f(x) (71), D the set of covectors satisfying (66). p.18: 'unlike those two inequalities [FO energy density, FK effective energy density], the QEI derived holds for any value of the coupling constant xi.' p.19: the bound is non-trivial in the sense of (74) and 'as this bound is derived by discarding positive terms we do not expect it to be optimal.' Left side is a DIFFERENCE: <:T_mn:>_psi = <T^ren>_psi - <T^ren>_psi0 (59), (65).
published_hypotheses: P1 (M,g) globally hyperbolic, time-oriented, n dimensions; QFT on a FIXED background (algebraic quantization, p.15)
P2 free real scalar field, mass m, coupling xi real, field equation (box_g + m^2 + xi R)phi = 0 (10) with box_g := -g^mn nabla nabla (p.5); conventions (-,+,+,+), MTW (+,+,+) (p.5)
P3 psi and the reference psi_0 Hadamard (p.16, (54)); W_0 the two-point function of psi_0; left side normal-ordered relative to psi_0 (59),(65)

P4 f real-valued, smooth, compactly supported in a SMALL SAMPLING DOMAIN: open subset contained in a globally hyperbolic convex normal neighbourhood, covered by one hyperbolic chart: d/dx^0 future-pointing timelike and c|u_0| >= sqrt(sum_j u_j^2) for every causal covector (66) (p.17, following Fewster-Smith [20])
P5 l^mu a null vector field defined in a neighbourhood of supp f (p.18)
P6 Leibniz rule for Wick powers, Hollands-Wald axiom 10, in the form (62)-(63) (p.17): a renormalization prescription assumed, not derived
P7 the point-split operator rho_hat_n = l.nabla (x) l.nabla is symmetric and of positive type, giving (70) (p.18, citing [7],[20])
Scope: any real xi (p.18); not optimal (p.19)

C2: FFKP's own steps (10),(11) take (9) to (12) in every term except the Ricci term: (9) - (12) = 2 xi R_mn phi^2 exactly -- a sign discrepancy in (12)/(13). C3: for T_ll = (1-2xi)A - 2xi B + k xi R_ll phi^2 the Leibniz/IBP step (62)-(63) gives Q[f] Ricci coefficient -k: eq.(9) -> -1, eq.(13) as printed -> +1, eq.(61) as extracted -> +2; printed (64)/(69b)/(72) carry +1/2, consistent with none; (63) verified as a total divergence. C4: on HPS g(l,l) = 0 exactly; R_ll = (f' r' - 2 f r'')/(f r) in general and -226800 pi^2 l^2 + O(l^4) with HPS boundary data (L = -2/3), equal to 8 pi (rho + p_l) of qeihps.py:174; hyperbolic-chart condition (66) satisfiable at the throat (c = 1.7169). lacked_data: Thm IV.1 is a mathematical theorem with no empirical input, so M's hypothesis in its data form does not bite: no measured datum enters (72) and none has moved (data_at_publication). What the authors did not have, and still nobody has, is the INPUT DATA to evaluate it on a specific curved background -- W_0 of a reference Hadamard state and <:phi^2:>_psi on HPS -- which is exactly why the tree's verdict is OPEN, and Kontou 2024 (Sec. 5.2) names the same absence. The one defect found is not a missing datum but an internal inconsistency in the v1 derivation (eq.(9) vs (12)/(13)/(61)/(64)): the Ricci coefficient in Q[f] printed as +1/2, where the conserved stress tensor of the paper's own action gives -1 (C1-C3). Evidence it matters: it is invisible in every application FFKP make (Minkowski DSNEC/SNEC, (75)-(93), R_mn = 0), which plausibly explains why it went unnoticed; evidence it matters for the tree: on HPS R_ll = -226800 pi^2 l^2 != 0 on any open supp f (C4b). Evidence against over-reading: no state violating the printed bound is exhibited (the bound is not sharp, p.19), the SciPost version is unread and may be corrected, and correcting the coefficient changes no verdict the tree draws from the theorem.
grade_evidence: What the tree uses 'in form' STANDS: any real xi (p.18 verbatim), small sampling domain, null l, the DIFFERENCE structure (59) -- all read at source and re-checked (C4a, C4d). The printed right side does NOT carry over to the tree's class: the v1 derivation supports Q[f] with Ricci coefficient +1/2 only where R_mn l^m l^n = 0 on supp f (or xi = 0), because eq.(9) -- shown here to be the conserved stress tensor of action (7) (C1a, residual 2e-165) -- leads to -1, and eqs.(12)/(13)/(61) as printed are inconsistent with both (C1b, C2, C3). HPS's throat neighbourhood is outside that class (R_ll = -226800 pi^2 l^2, C4b), and qeihps.py:99 copies the +1/2. This is a discrepancy in v1, recorded, not a refutation (no counterexample state; journal version unread; must not be quoted as an error in SciPost Phys. 16, 119 until that is read). Consequence for the tree: none on its verdicts -- VERDICT_APPLICABLE_QEI stays OPEN and KONTOU_REQUESTED_TEST_ON_HPS stays 'applies in form, not evaluable', since the blocking inputs (W_0, <:phi^2:> on HPS, HPS's state Hadamard) are untouched; only the Q[f] display at qeihps.py:99 carries a coefficient the source's own eq.(9) does not support.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: reading SciPost Phys. 16 (2024) 119 (or a v2) and finding (12)/(13)/(69b) corrected to the -1 coefficient consistent with (9) -- the theorem would then stand as the tree uses it in form, with the tree's display at qeihps.py:99 a stale copy. Also to STANDS: a convention under which both (9) and (12) hold together (none exists given (10)/(11), C2) or an error in C1 (re-run the script; it is exact differentiation evaluated at 30 digits). To WRONG: an explicit Hadamard state on a background with R_ll != 0 on supp f violating the printed (72) -- not attempted here, and not implied by the discrepancy since the bound is not sharp. To OPEN: if the journal version is shown to restate the theorem with a different Q[f] altogether whose derivation cannot be checked here.
